relevance_note: A systematic review of Danon disease that gives individual-level detail for a few previously published or registry patients, e.g. 'The fifth male patient carried a Trp321Arg missense mutation common to all isoforms^21'.
method_note: Narrative review; no patient table is in the converted text (Supplemental Tables 1 and 2 are referenced but not included; Table 2 cells are empty). JSON built by a short Python script from my own reading; no table transcribed. In scope: seven individuals with at least one individual-level fact (sex/age/variant/feature) in the text: refs 19, 18/20 (female carrier in the c.1150 G>C family), 21, 26, 33, 34, and one unpublished registry male (38 years, 'un-published data', labelled 'unnamed person 1'). Labels use the superscript reference number without the '^' conversion marker. Left out as count/group-level only: the four males of the c.1150 G>C family (only an average onset 54.2±13.8 years), the four of six affected Italian women who died suddenly (two with WPW and AV block, unnamed), Thiadens' male patients, the 2/7 case series, the two patients of ref 19 beyond the 4-month male, registry patients needing multiple ablations, and all cohort percentages. No variant rows for refs 19, 26, 33, 34 or the registry male: the text ties no printed variant to them. 'maculopathy,^34' in an eye-problem list was not attributed to the ref 34 patient. is_proband left null (review; no proband language). cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper is a review of published cases plus its own registry and makes no statement about re-reporting its own patients. Ref 21 patient's 'classic findings at age 21' recorded as onset (paragraph is about age of symptom onset). Ref 26 patient: '14-year old male ... at autopsy' recorded as deceased at P14Y; ventricular septal thickness 65 mm mapped to left ventricular hypertrophy. Ref 33: the authors note it is unclear whether the psychiatric episodes were related to Danon disease (also for the registry male). Ref 19 'severe obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy' mapped to LVH and LVOT obstruction on the checklist. No contradictions found.
